(Japanese: '''{{j|ポケモンセンターお{{ruby|姉|ねえ}}さん}}''' ''Pokémon Center lady''), also known as the '''Pokémon Center Nurse'''In the English versions of {{g|Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon}}, there is a set of Pokémon Center Nurse [[fashion item]]s. These are originally just '''{{j|ポケセン}}''' ''[[Pokémon Center|Pokécen]]'' fashion items in Japanese. or '''receptionist''' (Japanese: '''{{j|うけつけのねーちゃん}}''' ''reception lady''),In the [[Generation I]] games, {{game|Crystal}}, and {{game|FireRed and LeafGreen|s}}, the Pokémon Center ladies are referred to by some [[Non-player character|NPCs]] as receptionists (Japanese: '''{{j|うけつけのねーちゃん}}'''{{sup/1|RGBY}}{{sup/3|FRLG}} / '''{{j|うけつけのおねえさん}}'''{{sup/2|C}} ''reception lady''). In {{B2W2}}, they are called Pokémon Center receptionists ('''{{j|ポケモンセンターの{{ruby|受付|うけつけ}}の{{ruby|人|ひと}}}}''' ''Pokémon Center receptionist''). is an operator of a [[Pokémon Center]]. They facilitate the restoration of {{pkmn|Trainer}}s' {{OBP|Pokémon|species}} to full [[HP]], and usually provide this basic service free of charge. In {{game4|SMUSUM}}, they can be battled at the [[Battle Tree]] and [[Battle Royal Dome]] under the {{DL|Pokémon Trainer|Trainer class}} '''Pokémon Center Lady''' (Japanese: '''{{j|ＰＣおねえさん}}''' ''PC Lady''). In {{g|Legends: Z-A}}, they are referred to as the '''Pokémon Center clerk''',In {{g|Legends: Z-A}}, they are referred to as the "Pokémon Center clerk" during [[Mission (Legends: Z-A)|Side Mission 109: "Wondrous Self-Healing Pokémon"]]. In the Japanese version, they are simply described as ポケモンセンターのお姉さん ''the lady at the Pokémon Center''. and in addition to healing Pokémon, they sell [[item]]s commonly sold at [[Poké Mart]]s in other games. They can also be battled during the [[Z-A Royale]] under the {{DL|Pokémon Trainer|Trainer class}} '''Pokémon Center Clerk''' (Japanese: '''ポケセン受付嬢''' ''Pokémon Center Receptionist''). Among fans, the Pokémon Center lady is often mistaken for her counterpart introduced in ''[[Pokémon the Series]]'', [[Nurse Joy]]. ==In the core series== [[File:PokeCenter receptionist FRLG.png|thumb|left|The receptionist can heal the player's Pokémon]] [[File:Selene USUM Pokemon Center lady concept art.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ga|Selene}}'s nurse outfit in {{g|Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon}}]] A Pokémon Center lady operates every Pokémon Center in the [[Pokémon games]] (except the one in [[Po Town]], which was taken by [[Team Skull]]), usually standing behind the counter and beside a machine which is able to heal the {{player}}'s Pokémon to full health. ===Generation I=== In {{game|Yellow}}, their appearance was changed to simultaneously reflect the artwork and resemble [[Nurse Joy]] as she appears in [[Kanto]], the latter which was reinforced in {{LGPE}}. They are also all accompanied by {{p|Chansey}} like Nurse Joy. ===Generation II=== In the {{g|Gold and Silver Spaceworld '97 demo}}, the lady at the Pokémon Center in Silent Hill is unable to heal the player's Pokémon due to ongoing maintenance. In {{game2|Gold|Silver|Crystal}}, the lady in [[Fuchsia City]] has green hair instead of red. ===Generation IV=== In {{game2|Diamond|Pearl|Platinum}}, a lady named '''{{DL|Pokémon Super Contest|Casey}}''' (Japanese: '''{{j|メディ}}''' ''Medi'') participates in [[Rank (Contest)|Master Rank]] {{pkmn|Super Contest}}s with a Chansey [[nickname]]d '''Pinky''' (Japanese: '''{{j|ちゃんしー}}''' ''Chansey''). ===Generation V=== In {{B2W2}}, the player's {{OBP|mom|Black 2 and White 2}} used to be a Pokémon Center lady, outright stated by her during a [[Xtransceiver]] conversation.{{OBP|Mom|Black 2 and White 2}}: ''"Nimbasa City is the city of entertainment! Working at the Pokémon Center there was sure a lot of fun. [...]"'' ({{B2W2}}) She has mentioned working at [[Nimbasa City]] and is implied to have worked at [[Mistralton City]].{{OBP|Mom|Black 2 and White 2}}: ''"Mistralton City always makes me think of Skyla! People who had been hurt by the device in her Pokémon Gym would come to the Pokémon Center."'' ({{B2W2}}) ===Generation VI=== In {{g|Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire}}, there is an old lady on [[Mt. Chimney]] that states she used to be a "Pokémon Center girl".Old lady: ''"[...] Once a Pokémon Center girl, always a Pokémon Center girl! I’ll have your Pokémon in tip-top shape in a jiffy!"'' ({{g|Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire}}) ===Generation VII=== In {{game4|SMUSUM}}, Pokémon Center ladies named '''{{DL|List of Battle Royal Dome Trainers/Pokémon Center Lady|Mayu}}''' (Japanese: '''{{j|マッイ}}''' ''Ma'i'') and '''{{DL|List of Battle Tree Trainers/Pokémon Center Lady|Perri}}''' (Japanese: '''{{j|カマロリ}}''' ''Kamaloli'') appear as Trainers that the player can battle in the [[Battle Royal Dome]] and [[Battle Tree]] respectively. They don't specialize in any specific type, but they have a preference for pink Pokémon and those with support capabilities. They keep their Pokémon in [[Heal Ball]]s. In Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon, the player can [[Trainer customization|customize]] {{ga|Selene}} to wear a [[Fashion item|Pokémon Center Nurse outfit]]. This outfit can be obtained from the [[Game Freak]] offices in [[Heahea City]] after the credits. ===Generation VIII=== In {{g|Legends: Arceus}}, although there are no [[Pokémon Center]]s, [[Pesselle]] highly resembles the Pokémon Center lady and serves as the Captain of the [[Galaxy Team]]'s Medical Corps. ===Generation IX=== In {{g|Scarlet and Violet}}, the Pokémon Center lady in [[Mossui Town]] in [[Kitakami]] has a different design and dialogue from those in [[Paldea]]. She both speaks and dresses more informally and holds a [[Rotom Phone]] that she looks at when the player is not near her. If the player joins her behind the counter and talks to her, she will refuse to heal their Pokémon, telling them to talk to her from the other side of the counter. In the [[Mochi Mayhem]] epilogue, she is the only citizen of Mossui Town not afflicted by [[Mochi|Binding Mochi]] and has unique dialogue if spoken to at this point, warning the player of the strange occurrences in the town. [[Blueberry Academy]], on the other hand, has no Pokémon Centers or Pokémon Center ladies to attend them. Instead, there are self-service healing machines located across the [[Terarium]] for students, including the player, to use. In {{g|Legends: Z-A}}, the Pokémon Center clerks of [[Lumiose City]] sell [[item]]s in addition to healing Pokémon, offering goods such as [[Poké Ball]]s and [[Potion]]s like the [[Poké Mart]] in previous games. They also have a variety of different physical appearances, with distinct facial features and skin tones. A Pokémon Center clerk operates a traveling Pokémon Center stand on the north side of [[Rouge Plaza]], though she does not sell items. Early in the game, the lady operating the [[Vert District]] Pokémon Center installs the [[Pokédex]] app on the player's [[Rotom Phone]]. ===Pokémon=== {{Main|Pokémon Super Contest|section=Casey}} Model |} ==In animation== [[File:Nurse Joy JN.png|thumb|250px|[[Nurse Joy]] in {{aniseries|JN}}]]'' [[File:Mollie and Chansey.png|thumb|250px|[[Mollie]] and her {{TP|Mollie|Chansey}} in {{aniseries|HZ}}]] In {{aniseries|PTS}} and related media, the [[I Choose You! trilogy|''I Choose You!'' trilogy]], and {{aniseries|HZ}}, most Pokémon Centers are run by characters named '''[[Nurse Joy]]''' (Japanese: '''{{j|ジョーイ}}''' ''Joy'', referred to as '''{{j|ジョーイさん}}''' ''Joy-{{wp|Japanese honorifics#San|san}}'' by most characters). ===''Pokémon the Series''=== ===={{aniseries|SM}}==== In ''[[SM068|Real Life...Inquire Within!]]'', {{ash}} and {{ashcl}} substituted for [[Melemele Island]]'s Nurse Joy as part of a work experience program. During this, versions of the uniform intended for male operators were shown, and were worn by {{an|Kiawe}}, {{an|Sophocles}}, and (after clearing a misunderstanding) Ash as well. The male uniform appeared again in ''[[SM102|Alola, Alola!]]'', worn by {{an|Brock}} while he helped an ailing {{p|Yungoos}} as part of his {{tc|Doctor}} training. ===''Pokémon Horizons: The Series''=== [[File:Kitakami Pokémon Center lady anime.png|thumb|250px|A Pokémon Center lady in {{aniseries|HZ}}]]'' ====[[Mollie]]==== In {{aniseries|HZ}}, [[Mollie]] resembles a Pokémon Center lady, particularly those in [[Alola]], and originally assisted in Pokémon Centers and trained to become a {{tc|doctor}}, before deciding she wanted to travel and help [[wild Pokémon]] in need. Like Nurse Joy, she owns a {{TP|Mollie|Chansey}}. In ''[[HZ094|The Pokémon Center Lady]]'', it's revealed that [[Mollie's mother]] is an elderly Nurse Joy. ====Other==== In ''[[HZ070|Tinkatink's Hammer Wasn't Made in a Day]]'', a Pokémon Center lady from [[Kitakami]] was seen at [[Mossui Town]]. She does not bear a resemblance to Nurse Joy and instead resembles the Mossui Town Pokémon Center lady from [[The Teal Mask]]. She approached Mollie after seeing her performing medical procedures on the [[Countryside Harvest Festival]] participants. After exchanging a few words, the Pokémon Center lady injured her tooth with one of [[Murdock]]'s caramel apples. She reappeared in a flashback in ''[[HZ123|Mochi Mayhem!]]''. =====Voice actors===== {{vatable|color={{psychic color}}|bordercolor={{Y color dark}} |ja= 悠 社本 ''[[Haruka Shamoto]]'' }} ===Pokémon Origins=== Pokémon Center ladies made a couple of appearances during [[Pokémon Origins]], serving the same role as in the games. The first one was seen in [[Viridian City]] in ''[[PO01|File 1: Red]]'', while another one appeared in [[Lavender Town]] in ''[[PO02|File 2: Cubone]]''. Unlike in most other media, these ladies are different from each other, having different appearances and voices. ===Pokémon Generations=== Two Pokémon Center ladies from [[Lumiose City]] made a brief cameo appearance in the [[Pokémon Generations]] episode ''[[PG16|The Beauty Eternal]]'', where they were seen during a televised interview with [[Lysandre]]. Similar to Pokémon Origins, they have unique designs that differ from one another. ===Pokémon Evolutions=== A Pokémon Center lady appeared in a cameo in the [[Pokémon Evolutions]] episode ''[[PE01|The Champion]]''. Her outfit and appearance is the same as the Pokémon Center ladies in {{g|Sword and Shield}}. ===Gallery=== Pokémon Center lady PO.png|A Pokémon Center lady in [[Pokémon Origins]] Pokémon Center lady PG.png|Pokémon Center ladies in [[Pokémon Generations]] Pokémon Center Evolutions.png|A Pokémon Center lady in [[Pokémon Evolutions]] ==In the manga== [[File:Nurse Joy Golden Boys.png|thumb|150px|A Pokémon Center lady in [[Pokémon Gold & Silver: The Golden Boys]]]] ===The Electric Tale of Pikachu=== In addition to [[Nurse Joy]], several generic Pokémon Center ladies appear in [[The Electric Tale of Pikachu]], first appearing in ''[[ET03|Clefairy Tale]]''. They appear in a wide variety of outfits, which vary from city to city. ===Pokémon Adventures=== In ''[[PS015|Wartortle Wars]]'', a Pokémon Center lady at the [[Celadon City]] Pokémon Center healed {{adv|Red}}'s [[Pika]] while Red received a call from {{adv|Professor Oak}}. In ''[[PS585|Pinsir Changes]]'', a Pokémon Center lady at the [[Anistar City]] Pokémon Center was tied up as [[Emma|Essentia]] disguised as her to steal {{adv|Y}}'s [[Xerxer|Xerneas]]. Her appearance was based on the Pokémon Center lady within the [[Generation VI]] games. ===Pokémon Gold & Silver: The Golden Boys=== A Pokémon Center lady appeared in ''[[GB13|A Promise Given to Miltank]]''. {{-}} ==In the TCG== A {{TCG|Supporter card}} called {{TCG ID|Expedition|Pokémon Nurse|145}} appears in the {{TCG|Expedition Base Set}}. The art on this card slightly resembles [[Nurse Joy]] from the {{pkmn|animated series}}, but has blue hair. The nurse appearing on the card also seems to have been based on the games. A second card, titled {{TCG ID|Flashfire|Pokémon Center Lady|93}}, debuted in the {{TCG|Flashfire}} expansion, both as a regular print and a {{TCG|Full Art card}}.
